tensor_shape_limitation: Hook records a union, not per-image/warmup associations. Square TRAIN previews and rectangular diagnostic tensors are observed; causality for native-point error is unproven.
interpretation: Post-hoc descriptive grouping only. Still ordinals have no verified FPS/PTS, context IDs are not independent matches, and within-video pairs are correlated.

per_image.observation: The indoor blue-court left-side predictions are displaced strongly to image-right: P0/P4/P8/P10 and the near-left baseline slots lie inside the actual left lines. Right near-service P11 is almost coincident with G11; right baseline endpoints are much closer than the left endpoints. The predicted box still overlaps most of the court. This is asymmetric localization error rather than complete court absence.

The Monte Carlo clay view has a broadly recognizable court layout. Far baseline and service predictions sit slightly above the green line intersections, while near-left predictions lie left of GT. Errors are visibly moderate rather than a semantic index swap. This contrasts with larger left-side deformation in other clay stills.

The left baseline and service landmarks are displaced far to image-right, with far-side points also too low and near-left points too high. P0/P4/P8/P10 form an inner court boundary rather than the visible left boundary. The near-right service point remains close to its intersection. The box matches at IoU about0.814 despite severe point errors. The same pattern recurs in image20 from this publisher video.

On the indoor blue court, predicted far baseline points are above GT and predicted near baseline points are below GT. Far-left points also shift inward toward image-right. The near service line and its center are much closer. The prediction expands the court vertically around the middle region.

This second still from the same video as image1 repeats the left-side inward deformation, although its magnitude is lower. P0/P4/P8/P10 and near-left baseline points sit right of the real left intersections; right service points stay close. The predicted near baseline is also slightly too low.

The clay image has large rightward displacement of far-left and left service landmarks, and moderate rightward displacement of the service centers. Near-right service P11 is close. GT slot2 is null where the near-left player obscures the relevant area; its returned prediction is visible in the overlay but cannot be counted as hidden-point accuracy.

This clay view is one of the better localizations. Many service and baseline predictions are close to the visible intersections. Far baseline predictions remain somewhat high and the near-left service point is left of GT. Eleven of fourteen visible targets are within20pixels, so this is a relative success with residual error, not an exact calibration.

The camera framing has shifted horizontally compared with image6, yet the large left-side inward deformation persists. P0/P4/P8/P10 and near-left baseline points are displaced to image-right, while the near-right service point is much closer. GT slot3 is null at the near-right player; that slot remains excluded from localization targets.

This second still from the video of image7 is another relative success. The right-side baseline and service intersections and both service centers are close; the left baseline and left service points retain rightward offsets. Nine of fourteen visible targets are within20pixels, with mean error about15pixels, but left endpoints still prevent precise geometry.

Despite recognizable court extent, the left baseline and service predictions sit inside the actual court toward image-right. The right near-service point is comparatively close. This is the same Sonego/Khachanov visual court context as images2/19; localization quality varies substantially across these retained stills.

The indoor prediction places far baseline points too high and near baseline points too low, while service-center and near service-right points are much closer. Far-left and far-right coordinates also contract horizontally. This forms a vertically over-expanded outline rather than a uniform translation.

Far-left baseline and service points shift inward to image-right; far-right points shift somewhat inward to image-left. Far baseline predictions are high and near baseline predictions low. The right near-service and service-center region are relatively close. A similar pattern occurs in image17 from this video.

The indoor predicted far baseline lies above the visible baseline and the near baseline lies below it. Mid-court service points, especially the near center and near right, are much closer. The left far boundary shifts inward. Image18 from this video repeats the same broad error structure.

This still repeats the vertical expansion and inward far-left error of image4 from the same video. Predicted far baseline points remain above GT, predicted near baseline points below GT, while near service-center/right landmarks are closer. Player movement did not remove the retained geometric bias.

The same indoor court as image11 retains the over-expanded vertical extent: the predicted near baseline is below the visible baseline and the far baseline above it. Near service-center P13 is nearly coincident with G13, showing that good middle points coexist with inaccurate outer extents.

No court instance or keypoint prediction is returned. The saved image is a normal elevated clay singles view with the court lines visible and fourteen visible GT labels. It is not a blank frame or an obvious close-up. All fourteen visible targets correctly remain misses; this review cannot identify the cause of the failure from one still.

The far-left baseline and service landmarks are noticeably right of their GT intersections; far-right points are closer. The predicted near baseline sits below GT, and near-left points also move inward. The near-right service point remains close. It resembles image12 but with larger left-side errors.

This indoor image repeats the pattern in image13: far baseline predictions too high, near baseline predictions too low, and far-left points shifted inward. Service-center and near-right service predictions are much closer. The repeated view supports an error-pattern grouping, not a claim of independent temporal stability.

The large left-side displacement reverses direction here: far-left, near-left and left service predictions fall to image-left of GT, with far-side points also too high. The right near-service point stays close, and the box still matches. This rules out describing the entire sample as one constant rightward translation or applying an ad-hoc coordinate offset.

This still strongly repeats image3: the left-side points lie far inside the court toward image-right, far points are too low, and the near-right service point is close. The same video supplies both large-error frames. Similar predictions on the paired stills show repeated deformation in this retained development view, not qualified video stability.
